meta.title: Lerche Aerostat · Balloon ascents to 25,000 m
meta.description: A six-hour ascent to the stratosphere beneath a helium balloon. Six guests, one pilot, no rocket. Launch windows 2027, from €128,000 per seat.

ui.ascent: The ascent, from the launch field to 25,000 metres

stations.label: Launch field
stations.title: Rise with the sun.
stations.body: Six hours beneath a helium balloon, to 25,000 metres. Six guests, one pilot, no rocket.

stations.label: Lift-off
stations.title: You leave at the pace of a bicycle.
stations.body: Five metres a second. No thrust and no noise: the field simply gets smaller. The envelope above you is a slack column of film, with a single bubble of helium at its crown.

stations.label: Breakfast
stations.title: Breakfast above the weather.
stations.body: The cloud deck closes underneath and the sun comes up from below it. The table is laid at five thousand metres and cleared before ten.

stations.label: Above the airliners
stations.title: Every airliner is now below you.
stations.body: Outside it is minus fifty-six. The helium has expanded to more than three times its launch volume, and the envelope is filling out.

stations.label: The capsule
stations.title: A room with one continuous window.

stations.label: Black sky
stations.title: The sky goes dark while the sun is shining.
stations.body: Ninety-six per cent of the atmosphere is beneath you. What is left of it is the thin blue line on the horizon.

stations.label: Float
stations.title: Float.
stations.body: Two hours at 25,000 metres. Drag sideways to look around.

hours.title: Six hours, most of them spent looking.
hours.aria: Altitude over time: 83 minutes up, two hours level at 25,000 metres, two hours down.

legs.name: Lift-off
legs.note: Before first light, when the air on the field is still.

legs.name: Float
legs.note: Ascent at 5 m/s. Sunrise meets you at about 5,000 m.

legs.name: Descent begins
legs.note: Two hours level. The pilot valves helium to start down.

legs.name: Parafoil
legs.note: The envelope is released and a steerable wing takes over.

legs.name: Touchdown
legs.note: Ground crew has followed by road. Lunch is at the field.

Pre-flight briefing and cabin fitting with your pilot
A second launch window at no charge if weather scrubs the first

items.a: No. Space begins at about 100 km and we float at 25 km. You are above 96 per cent of the atmosphere, the sky is black and the horizon is curved, but you remain in the stratosphere.
No. The capsule rises and descends gently, so you feel your normal weight the whole way. You can stand, walk around the cabin and eat at a table.
Anyone who is fit to take a commercial flight. The cabin is kept at sea-level pressure and room temperature, so there is no suit and no training beyond the briefing.
We launch only in calm air at the field. If the window is scrubbed, your seat moves to the next window of your choice at no charge.
The pilot releases helium to begin the descent. At about 3,000 m the envelope is let go and a steerable parafoil carries the capsule to a prepared landing zone.
Yes, a private one, with a window.
